title: Notre année scientifique en révision
oneGoal: Students will identify and recall the main science topics they explored during the year

opening.activity: Welcome circle and year overview introduction
opening.visualSupports: Timeline display of the school year with science unit photos

main.activity: Interactive science year review using timeline and memory sharing
main.visualSupports: Visual timeline with unit icons and key vocabulary cards

decisionPoints.question: What science topics were most memorable for students this year?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on those topics for deeper recall and connection
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use visual prompts and peer sharing to activate memories

decisionPoints.question: Should we use a timeline format or topic-by-topic review?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Continue with chronological timeline approach
decisionPoints.ifNo: Switch to thematic groupings of similar concepts

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to make connections between different science units?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Guide students to find links between units
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on individual unit recall before making connections

closing.activity: Share one favorite science memory with the class
closing.assessment: Observation of student ability to recall and articulate science experiences

troubleshooting.then: use visual prompts, peer partnerships, and journal browsing to support recall

realWorldConnection: Reflecting on learning helps us understand how much we've grown, like looking at photos from the beginning of the year

title: Nos découvertes les plus excitantes
oneGoal: Students will identify their most exciting scientific discoveries from the year and explain why they were special

opening.activity: Review previous lesson and introduce the concept of scientific discoveries
opening.visualSupports: Images of famous scientific discoveries adapted for Grade 1

main.activity: Individual reflection and small group sharing of most exciting science discoveries
main.visualSupports: Sentence starters and emotion words display

decisionPoints.question: Should students share discoveries individually or in small groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use individual presentation format with audience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep to small group sharing for comfort and time management

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students who struggle to identify favorite discoveries?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide guided prompts and visual reminders of activities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use peer partnerships to help generate ideas together

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to explain their thinking or should we focus on sharing experiences?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include 'why' questions in sharing prompts
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on describing what happened and how it felt

closing.activity: Gallery walk of discovery drawings with positive comments
closing.assessment: Observe student ability to identify personally meaningful learning moments

troubleshooting.then: encourage choosing one for now and saving others for later lessons

realWorldConnection: Scientists often share their most exciting discoveries with others, just like we share exciting news with friends

title: Qu'est-ce qu'une exposition scientifique?
oneGoal: Students will understand what a science fair or exposition is and how scientists share their work

opening.activity: Connect sharing discoveries to the idea of science exhibitions
opening.visualSupports: Age-appropriate images of children at science fairs and exhibitions

main.activity: Explore the concept of science sharing through videos, pictures, and role-play
main.visualSupports: Simple flowchart showing: Learn → Practice → Share → Celebrate

decisionPoints.question: Should we show examples of science fairs or focus on simple sharing concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use carefully selected, age-appropriate science fair videos
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on familiar sharing experiences like show-and-tell

decisionPoints.question: How can we make the concept accessible without overwhelming students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use simple analogies and familiar sharing situations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Break down the concept into very small, concrete steps

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready to understand audience or should we focus on showing work?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include discussion about who comes to see science work
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus mainly on the act of showing what we've learned

closing.activity: Practice being a science audience for teacher demonstration
closing.assessment: Note student understanding of basic science sharing concepts

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: understanding the concept of formal presentation
troubleshooting.then: relate to familiar experiences like birthday parties or school concerts

realWorldConnection: Understanding how people share their best work at art shows, school concerts, or sports games

title: Choisir notre projet de démonstration
oneGoal: Students will select one science topic or experiment from the year to demonstrate at the exposition

opening.activity: Review science year and introduce project selection
opening.visualSupports: Visual menu of science topics studied this year with pictures

main.activity: Individual reflection and selection process with teacher conferences
main.visualSupports: Decision-making criteria poster: Safe, Fun, I Know It Well

decisionPoints.question: Should students choose individually or work in small groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow individual choice with option for partnerships
decisionPoints.ifNo: Organize into predetermined small groups with shared choices

decisionPoints.question: What criteria should guide project selection (interest, success, safety)?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use all three criteria in a simple checklist format
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on student interest and engagement level

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent choice or need guided options?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide full menu of year's topics for selection
decisionPoints.ifNo: Pre-select 4-5 most appropriate options for students to choose from

closing.activity: Share chosen project with a partner and explain why
closing.assessment: Document student project choices and reasoning

troubleshooting.then: use elimination process and 'gut feeling' check to narrow choices

realWorldConnection: Making choices about what to share, like picking our best artwork for a family display

title: Planifier notre démonstration
oneGoal: Students will create a simple plan for how they will show their chosen science topic to visitors

opening.activity: Review chosen projects and introduce planning concepts
opening.visualSupports: Simple planning template with pictures: What? How? What do I need?

main.activity: Create individual planning sheets with drawings and simple steps
main.visualSupports: Step-by-step planning process poster and sample completed plans

decisionPoints.question: Should we provide planning templates or encourage creative formats?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide basic template but allow creative additions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Start with completely open-ended planning approach

decisionPoints.question: How detailed should the planning be for Grade 1 students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include 3-4 simple steps with drawings
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on just the main idea and one key step

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for thinking about audience needs or focus on their own presentation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include 'What will visitors see?' in planning
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on 'What will I do?' for now

closing.activity: Partner sharing of plans with feedback and suggestions
closing.assessment: Review planning sheets for clarity and feasibility

troubleshooting.then: use think-aloud modeling and break into very small actions

realWorldConnection: Planning how to explain something to others, like teaching a game to a younger child

title: Matériel et outils nécessaires
oneGoal: Students will identify and gather the materials they need for their science demonstration

opening.activity: Review plans and introduce material identification
opening.visualSupports: Safety symbol chart and material category pictures

main.activity: Create material lists and practice safe handling procedures
main.visualSupports: Material safety chart with green, yellow, and red categories

decisionPoints.question: Which materials are safe and appropriate for student-led demonstrations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow all green-category materials with student responsibility
decisionPoints.ifNo: Restrict to pre-approved safe materials list only

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on simple materials or allow more complex tools with supervision?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include some yellow-category materials with adult helper assigned
decisionPoints.ifNo: Stick to simple, completely safe materials students can handle alone

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for material responsibility or need teacher-prepared sets?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Have students gather and organize their own materials
decisionPoints.ifNo: Pre-prepare material sets with student input on arrangement

closing.activity: Practice setup and cleanup procedures with materials
closing.assessment: Observe student understanding of material safety and organization

troubleshooting.then: create visual checklist and practice run-through with materials

realWorldConnection: Getting ready for activities by gathering what we need, like packing for a trip or preparing for cooking

title: Pratiquer notre explication simple
oneGoal: Students will practice explaining their science topic using simple words that other children can understand

opening.activity: Warm-up with simple explanation practice using familiar objects
opening.visualSupports: Simple explanation framework: This is... It does... I like it because...

main.activity: Practice rounds with partners, focusing on clear, simple language
main.visualSupports: Word choice helper chart: hard words → easy words

decisionPoints.question: Should students practice with peers or adults first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with peer practice for comfort level
decisionPoints.ifNo: Begin with adult practice for immediate feedback

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students use age-appropriate vocabulary?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide word substitution chart and practice
decisionPoints.ifNo: Model simple language and have students repeat

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for feedback on their explanations or need encouragement first?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include gentle, specific feedback with encouragement
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus purely on positive reinforcement and building confidence

closing.activity: One-minute explanation challenge with whole group audience
closing.assessment: Note clarity of explanations and comfort level with presenting

troubleshooting.then: practice explaining to a stuffed animal or younger child first

realWorldConnection: Learning to explain things clearly so others understand, like telling someone how to play our favorite game

title: Créer un affichage visuel
oneGoal: Students will create a simple visual display (drawing, poster, or model) to support their science demonstration

opening.activity: Look at examples of visual displays and discuss their purpose
opening.visualSupports: Gallery of age-appropriate science displays with features highlighted

main.activity: Create individual visual displays with choice of format and materials
main.visualSupports: Visual display planning template and design idea examples

decisionPoints.question: What visual formats are most appropriate for Grade 1 science concepts?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow choice between drawing, simple poster, or basic model
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on drawings with labels as the primary format

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on drawings, simple posters, or 3D models?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Offer all three options based on student project needs
decisionPoints.ifNo: Standardize on one format for consistency and time management

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent creation or need guided templates?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide optional templates but encourage creative additions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use structured templates with specific areas for student input

closing.activity: Gallery walk with positive feedback on visual displays
closing.assessment: Evaluate visual displays for clarity and connection to science topic

troubleshooting.ifStrugglingWith: knowing what to include in display
troubleshooting.then: use guiding questions: What? How? Why is it cool?

realWorldConnection: Using pictures and displays to help explain ideas, like showing photos when telling about vacation

title: Questions que les visiteurs pourraient poser
oneGoal: Students will anticipate and practice answering simple questions about their science topic

opening.activity: Introduce the idea of visitor questions through role-play
opening.visualSupports: Common question types poster with picture cues

main.activity: Generate possible questions and practice answering with partners
main.visualSupports: Answer framework: I think... because... Do you want to see?

decisionPoints.question: What types of questions are most likely from different age groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice with age-specific question categories
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on general curiosity questions regardless of age

decisionPoints.question: Should we practice specific questions or general question-answering skills?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Create specific question bank for each project type
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on general questioning strategies and comfort building

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for unknown questions or should we stick to predictable ones?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include some surprise questions in practice
decisionPoints.ifNo: Practice only with predictable, prepared questions

closing.activity: Quick question-answer rounds with the whole class as visitors
closing.assessment: Observe student comfort level and ability to respond to questions

troubleshooting.then: practice saying 'That's a great question! Let me think...' or 'I'm not sure, but I know...'

realWorldConnection: Being ready to answer questions about things we know well, like explaining our favorite books or toys

title: Sécurité pendant notre démonstration
oneGoal: Students will identify and practice safety rules for their science demonstration with visitors

opening.activity: Review general safety rules and apply them to demonstration contexts
opening.visualSupports: Safety rules poster with pictures and symbols

main.activity: Create personalized safety checklists and practice safety procedures
main.visualSupports: Safety action cards: Stop, Look, Think, Ask

decisionPoints.question: Which safety considerations are most important for student-led demonstrations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on material handling and visitor guidance safety
decisionPoints.ifNo: Concentrate on basic personal safety and space organization

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on material safety or visitor safety protocols?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include both with emphasis on visitor safety
decisionPoints.ifNo: Prioritize material safety as the foundation

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for safety leadership or need adult supervision reminders?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Practice student safety leadership with backup adult support
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on recognizing when to call for adult help

closing.activity: Safety scenario practice with problem-solving discussions
closing.assessment: Check student understanding of safety priorities and procedures

troubleshooting.then: create visual safety reminder cards and practice calm breathing

realWorldConnection: Being responsible for safety when showing others our activities, like teaching someone to ride a bike safely

title: Première pratique complète
oneGoal: Students will perform a complete run-through of their science demonstration with classmates as audience

opening.activity: Setup demonstration spaces and review practice expectations
opening.visualSupports: Practice checklist and supportive audience behavior chart

main.activity: Full demonstration practice with structured audience feedback
main.visualSupports: Audience job chart: Listen, Look, Think of kind words

decisionPoints.question: Should students present individually or in small groups?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use individual presentations with small audience rotation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Organize small group presentations with larger audiences

decisionPoints.question: How can we provide supportive feedback without discouraging students?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use structured positive feedback with one gentle suggestion
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus purely on encouragement and celebration of efforts

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for peer feedback or should we focus on teacher observation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include guided peer feedback with kind word focus
decisionPoints.ifNo: Have teacher provide all feedback while peers practice audience skills

closing.activity: Celebration circle sharing what went well and how students felt
closing.assessment: Document demonstration readiness and areas needing support

troubleshooting.then: provide calm-down strategies and extra practice opportunities

realWorldConnection: Practicing performances before the real event, like rehearsing for a school play or music concert

title: Améliorer notre présentation
oneGoal: Students will identify one specific improvement they can make to their science demonstration

opening.activity: Reflect on practice session and introduce improvement mindset
opening.visualSupports: Growth mindset poster: Good → Better → Best!

main.activity: Self-reflection and improvement planning with teacher conferences
main.visualSupports: Improvement areas chart: Louder voice, Clearer words, Better showing

decisionPoints.question: Should improvements focus on content clarity or presentation skills?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow student choice between content and delivery improvements
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on presentation skills as more immediately achievable

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students identify achievable improvements?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide specific, small-step improvement options to choose from
decisionPoints.ifNo: Guide students to very specific, single-focus improvements

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for self-reflection or need guided improvement suggestions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Start with self-reflection then confirm with teacher guidance
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide teacher-identified improvements with student input

closing.activity: Practice improved element with a partner for immediate feedback
closing.assessment: Note student ability to identify and work on specific improvements

troubleshooting.then: use video replay or peer observations to identify growth opportunities

realWorldConnection: Making things better through practice and changes, like improving at sports or drawing

title: Aider les autres avec leurs projets
oneGoal: Students will provide helpful feedback and encouragement to classmates preparing their demonstrations

opening.activity: Discuss what helpful feedback looks like and practice kind words
opening.visualSupports: Helpful helper chart: Listen, Think, Say something kind and helpful

main.activity: Structured peer feedback sessions with rotation and guided prompts
main.visualSupports: Feedback sentence starters: I liked... You could try... Great job with...

decisionPoints.question: What feedback skills are appropriate for Grade 1 students to practice?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Focus on specific positive observations and gentle suggestions
decisionPoints.ifNo: Concentrate only on positive encouragement and celebration

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on positive comments or specific suggestions?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance positive comments with one gentle suggestion
decisionPoints.ifNo: Emphasize positive comments with optional suggestions

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for peer evaluation or should we model supportive language?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow guided peer evaluation with supportive language frames
decisionPoints.ifNo: Have teacher model supportive language while students practice listening

closing.activity: Thank-you circle where students appreciate help received from others
closing.assessment: Observe student ability to give and receive constructive feedback

troubleshooting.then: provide specific sentence frames and model examples

realWorldConnection: Helping friends get better at things they're working on, like cheering each other on during games

title: Inviter notre famille
oneGoal: Students will create invitations for their families to attend the science exposition

opening.activity: Discuss family celebration and the importance of sharing learning
opening.visualSupports: Family words chart and invitation template examples

main.activity: Create personalized family invitations with drawings and key information
main.visualSupports: Invitation checklist: Who, What, When, Where, Why

decisionPoints.question: Should invitations include specific details about student demonstrations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Include brief description of student's project on invitation
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep invitations general with focus on celebration aspect

decisionPoints.question: How can we make invitations accessible for all family situations?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use multiple language options and flexible wording about family
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use simple universal language about 'special people' instead of specific family terms

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for writing invitations or should we use templates/dictation?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide writing templates with student choice in personalization
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use teacher/student dictated text with student art additions

closing.activity: Share invitations with partners and practice explaining the event
closing.assessment: Check invitation completeness and student excitement about sharing

troubleshooting.then: use guided questions to help students think through invitation details

realWorldConnection: Inviting people we care about to see our special work, like asking grandparents to come to graduation

title: Préparer notre espace d'exposition
oneGoal: Students will organize their demonstration space and materials for the science exposition

opening.activity: Tour exposition space and discuss organization principles
opening.visualSupports: Space organization examples and setup checklist

main.activity: Set up individual demonstration spaces with materials and displays
main.visualSupports: Space setup diagram and material organization chart

decisionPoints.question: How much space and setup responsibility can Grade 1 students handle?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Give students full responsibility for their defined space
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide structured setup tasks with adult support available

decisionPoints.question: Should we focus on individual spaces or collaborative classroom setup?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Organize individual spaces within collaborative room setup
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on individual spaces with minimal room-wide coordination

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent organization or need step-by-step guidance?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide setup checklist and allow independent organization
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use step-by-step guided setup with teacher direction

closing.activity: Space walk-through and final setup adjustments
closing.assessment: Check space organization and student readiness for event

troubleshooting.then: provide specific placement guides and practice setup routine

realWorldConnection: Getting ready for special events by organizing our space, like setting up for a birthday party

title: Répétition générale
oneGoal: Students will perform a final practice run of their science demonstration with timing and setup

opening.activity: Final preparation check and confidence building activities
opening.visualSupports: Final preparation checklist and confidence affirmation cards

main.activity: Complete dress rehearsal with timing, setup, and audience simulation
main.visualSupports: Performance flow chart and timing guidelines

decisionPoints.question: Should the dress rehearsal include other classes as audience?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Invite other classes for authentic audience experience
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use classroom-only rehearsal to maintain comfort level

decisionPoints.question: How can we address last-minute concerns without creating anxiety?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Address concerns individually with calm problem-solving
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on positive reinforcement and confidence building

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for independent performance or need support reminders?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Allow independent performance with minimal prompting
decisionPoints.ifNo: Provide discrete support cues and encouragement throughout

closing.activity: Celebration of readiness and final encouragement circle
closing.assessment: Final readiness check and confidence level assessment

troubleshooting.then: provide calming strategies and focus on fun aspects of sharing

realWorldConnection: Final practice before important events to make sure everything goes smoothly, like rehearsing before performing

title: Notre exposition scientifique!
oneGoal: Students will successfully demonstrate their science learning to visitors at the exposition event

opening.activity: Final setup, calm preparation, and welcome visitors
opening.visualSupports: Welcome display and student confidence reminders

main.activity: Active science exposition with student demonstrations to family and community visitors
main.visualSupports: Station guides and visitor flow directions

decisionPoints.question: How can we support nervous students during the actual event?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide discrete teacher support and calm encouragement
decisionPoints.ifNo: Use peer buddy system and confident student helpers

decisionPoints.question: Should students rotate as both presenters and audience members?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Plan rotation schedule for students to see other presentations
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep students focused on their own demonstrations throughout

decisionPoints.question: How do we ensure every student feels successful regardless of performance?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Celebrate effort and participation rather than performance quality
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on individual growth and personal achievement recognition

closing.activity: Thank visitors, celebration of accomplishment, and cleanup
closing.assessment: Observe successful participation and celebrate all student efforts

troubleshooting.then: provide quiet space option and emphasize that participation is the success

title: Célébrer nos réussites
oneGoal: Students will reflect on their successful participation in the science exposition and celebrate their growth

opening.activity: Celebration circle sharing favorite moments from the exposition
opening.visualSupports: Photo display from the exposition event

main.activity: Individual and group reflection on growth, learning, and accomplishments
main.visualSupports: Growth comparison charts and accomplishment celebration display

decisionPoints.question: Should celebration focus on individual achievements or collective success?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Balance individual recognition with group celebration
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus primarily on collective class accomplishment

decisionPoints.question: How can we help students identify specific growth and learning?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use before/after comparisons and specific skill identification
decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus on general feelings of accomplishment and pride

decisionPoints.question: Are students ready for formal reflection or should we use informal sharing?
decisionPoints.ifYes: Use guided reflection activities with sharing opportunities
decisionPoints.ifNo: Keep to informal celebration and story sharing

closing.activity: Class celebration with recognition of everyone's unique contribution
closing.assessment: Document student recognition of personal growth and learning

troubleshooting.then: use specific examples and peer recognition to highlight individual progress

realWorldConnection: Feeling proud of accomplishments and recognizing how much we've learned and grown

title: Apprendre des autres projets

opening.visualSupports: Photo gallery of all student projects from the exposition

main.activity: Structured sharing about what students learned from classmates' projects

decisionPoints.ifYes: Provide guided observation questions with free sharing time

decisionPoints.ifNo: Focus purely on appreciation and positive observations

closing.activity: Create thank-you notes or appreciation messages for classmates
closing.assessment: Note student ability to recognize and appreciate diverse approaches to science

troubleshooting.then: use photos and documentation to prompt memories and observations
